readings: Join fees to their orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`; drop fees with no matching order) and group by time in force (`orders.timespan`). For each group, find the average `rebrate` / `feerate` ratio (ignoring missing values) and how many order matches it has. Keep only the groups whose match count is strictly above the average match count across all groups. For those groups, give me one row: the average of their average ratios, the total of their match counts, and the average amount by which their match count exceeds that cross-group average. No rounding.
queries:
WITH grouped AS (
  SELECT
    o.timespan,
    AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio,
    COUNT(*) AS match_count
  FROM fees AS f
  JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
cross_group AS (
  SELECT AVG(match_count) AS avg_match_count
  FROM grouped
)
SELECT
  AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio,
  SUM(g.match_count) AS total_match_count,
  AVG(g.match_count - c.avg_match_count) AS avg_excess_match_count
FROM grouped AS g
CROSS JOIN cross_group AS c
WHERE g.match_count > c.avg_match_count
